LLM_description:
Situation:
Enemy interdiction and indirect fire have disrupted lines of communication feeding forward elements from multiple regional depots. Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Node Echo remain operational but are constrained by daily issue limits and variable reception capacity. Routes through the valley corridor are exposed to ambush and improvised explosive devices; the river road requires engineer clearance for bridge approaches; the ridge line route is open but weather-prone. Forward Operating Base Alpha, Outpost Sierra, and other maneuver elements report rising consumption of ammunition, rations, and medical materiel. Movement control teams require synchronized convoy dispatches to reduce exposure and deconflict traffic.

Mission:
Resupply designated units from available depots across the planning window, meeting operational demand while minimizing total cost. The objective is to balance transport costs, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs associated with route activation.

Execution/Concept:
- Flows will be planned from each depot to each unit by supply type and day. Outbound dispatches from each depot must remain within that depot’s daily supply availability for each item.  
- Unit demands must be satisfied by inbound flows; any authorized shortfall will be recorded as slack and incur shortage penalties. Slack is an exception, not a default planning mechanism.  
- Vehicle loading is constrained by capacity. Cargo allocation will account for the volumetric or weight footprint of each supply line item to ensure no vehicle exceeds capacity.  
- Vehicles can only move on routes that are intentionally activated. Activating a route—sending any vehicles at all—incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, UAV overwatch, and communications/electronic warfare support), regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route.  
- Total vehicles available per day are limited by the fleet cap. Vehicle assignments across all routes and depots must not exceed the fleet limit.  
- Transport costs vary by depot–unit pairing and day; planners will consolidate shipments to reduce the number of activated routes, prioritize lower-risk corridors when feasible, and time movements to exploit weather and security windows.  
- Depots with more secure access may stage cargo for onward movement to forward supply points to mitigate risk without breaching capacity constraints.  
- If risk or capacity makes full delivery infeasible, accept minimal slack only where penalty costs are lower than cumulative transport, vehicle, and route activation costs under current threat conditions.  
- Movement coordination with engineers and security elements will be integrated into route activation decisions to ensure risk is appropriately priced and minimized.
